findings.title: Options-object calls enable rejectOnClear by default
findings.cause: When the argument is an options object, line 7 destructures `rejectOnClear = true` even though the public API documents the default as `false`.
findings.impact: Callers using the documented `pLimit({concurrency: 1})` form now get rejected pending promises from `clearQueue()` instead of the previous discard-without-rejection behavior. This can surface unexpected AbortError failures in shutdown paths and Promise.all consumers.
findings.evidence: Source: `index.js:6-8` sets the object default to true and `index.js:77-88` rejects queued promises when `rejectOnClear` is truthy. Contract: `readme.md:46-52`, `readme.md:149-155`, and `index.d.ts:99-106` all say `rejectOnClear` is boolean with default false. Probe output: `object-default-clearQueue-outcome { state: 'rejected', name: 'AbortError', message: 'This operation was aborted' }`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run the targeted Node probe used in this audit: load `index.js` with a minimal in-memory Queue stub, call `const limit = pLimit({concurrency: 1}); const running = limit(() => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 40))); const pending = limit(() => 'pending-result'); await Promise.resolve(); limit.clearQueue();` and observe `pending` rejects with AbortError. A regression test should assert the promise remains pending/discarded unless `{rejectOnClear: true}` is passed.

findings.title: Falsy non-boolean rejectOnClear values bypass validation
findings.cause: Line 12 checks `rejectOnClear && typeof rejectOnClear !== 'boolean'`, so only truthy non-boolean values throw. Falsy non-booleans such as `0`, `''`, and `null` are accepted.
findings.impact: The runtime contract no longer matches the documented and typed boolean option. Invalid configuration can silently change queue-clearing behavior instead of failing fast, making JavaScript consumers behave differently from TypeScript consumers.
findings.evidence: Source: `index.js:12-14`. Contract: `readme.md:46-52` and `index.d.ts:99-106` define `rejectOnClear` as boolean. The repository type test only covers a truthy string at `index.test-d.ts:29`, leaving falsy invalid values untested. Probe output: `rejectOnClear-invalid-accepted 0`, `rejectOnClear-invalid-accepted ""`, and `rejectOnClear-invalid-accepted null`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add runtime assertions that `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: 0})`, `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: ''})`, and `pLimit({concurrency: 1, rejectOnClear: null})` throw the same TypeError as a truthy invalid value.

findings.title: limit.map drops the index for non-array iterables
findings.cause: Lines 108-112 special-case arrays and pass `undefined` as the mapper index for every non-array iterable.
findings.impact: Documented support for iterables is now inconsistent: arrays receive `(value, index)`, while Sets, generators, and iterator objects receive `(value, undefined)`. Any mapper that keys output, applies per-position delays, or preserves positional metadata breaks for supported iterable inputs.
findings.evidence: Source: `index.js:108-112`. Contract: `readme.md:78-85` and `index.d.ts:30-43` state the mapper receives the item value and its index and is equivalent to `Array.from(iterable, (item, index) => limit(mapperFunction, item, index))`. Probe output for `new Set(['a', 'b'])`: `set-map-indexes [["a",null],["b",null]]` where JSON `null` represents the passed `undefined` index.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Run `await pLimit(1).map(new Set(['a', 'b']), (value, index) => [value, index])`; expected `[['a', 0], ['b', 1]]`, actual indexes are `undefined`. Extend the existing Set/iterator tests to assert the second mapper argument.

findings.title: limitFunction no longer forwards call arguments
findings.cause: Line 124 returns a zero-argument wrapper and invokes `function_()` instead of forwarding `...arguments_` from the limited function call.
findings.impact: Every `limitFunction` consumer whose wrapped function needs inputs now receives `undefined` values. This breaks the exported TypeScript signature, README recipe, benchmark scenario, and normal uses such as `urls.map(url => limitedFetchUrl(url))`.
findings.evidence: Source: `index.js:121-125`. Contract: `index.d.ts:133-136` returns `(...arguments_: Arguments) => Promise<ReturnType>`, and `recipes.md:144-163` demonstrates `limitedFetchUrl(url)`. The benchmark also calls `limitedTask(delay, i)` at `benchmark.js:193-194`. Probe output: `limitFunction-args undefined:undefined` for a wrapped `(first, second) => `${first}:${second}` called as `limited('left', 'right')`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add a test such as `const limited = limitFunction(async (a, b) => `${a}:${b}`, {concurrency: 1}); t.is(await limited('left', 'right'), 'left:right');`. Current runtime returns `undefined:undefined`.

findings.title: Infinity concurrency is rejected despite established support
findings.cause: Line 128 now requires `Number.isInteger(concurrency) && concurrency > 0`, removing the previous explicit allowance for `Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY`.
findings.impact: Consumers using `pLimit(Infinity)` or setting `limit.concurrency = Infinity` as an unlimited/pass-through mode now receive a TypeError. This is a regression from the repository baseline and from the error text/API framing of accepting a number from 1 and up.
findings.evidence: Source: `index.js:127-130` rejects non-integers. Baseline comparison from `git show HEAD:index.js` shows the previous validator allowed `(Number.isInteger(concurrency) || concurrency === Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY) && concurrency > 0`. Probe output: `infinity-concurrency rejected Expected `concurrency` to be a number from 1 and up`.
findings.reproduction_or_test: Add tests asserting `pLimit(Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY)` constructs a limiter and `limit.concurrency = Number.POSITIVE_INFINITY` is accepted. Current code throws the TypeError in both paths.
